target.title: fix(gateway): require shared secret for tailscale serve auth
target.body:
## Summary
Fixes #57110.

Adds an opt-in `gateway.auth.requireTailscaleSharedSecret` setting for Tailscale Serve Control UI/WebSocket access. When enabled, a remote Control UI WebSocket request must pass verified Tailscale identity and the configured token or password before it is accepted, and toggling the setting at runtime invalidates Tailscale-authenticated sessions established under the previous policy.

## Root cause
`src/gateway/auth.ts:598` kept the existing tokenless Tailscale Serve path separate from shared-secret auth:

```before
if (canUseTailscaleHeaderAuth && !hasExplicitSharedSecretAuth(connectAuth)) {
  const tailscaleCheck = await resolveVerifiedTailscaleUser({
    req,
    tailscaleWhois,
  });
  if (tailscaleCheck.ok) {
    limiter?.reset(ip, rateLimitScope);
    return {
      ok: true,
      method: "tailscale",
      user: tailscaleCheck.user.login,
    };
  }
}
```

There was no accepted config field that required both verified Tailscale Serve identity and the configured Gateway shared secret.

## Fix
`src/gateway/auth.ts:574` now handles the opt-in layered path before the tokenless Tailscale branch:

```after
if (canUseTailscaleHeaderAuth && auth.requireTailscaleSharedSecret === true) {
  const tailscaleCheck = await resolveVerifiedTailscaleUser({
    req,
    tailscaleWhois,
  });
  if (!tailscaleCheck.ok) {
    return tailscaleCheck;
  }
  const sharedSecretResult = authorizeSharedSecretAuth({
    auth,
    connectAuth,
    limiter,
    ip,
    rateLimitScope,
  });
  if (!sharedSecretResult.ok) {
    return sharedSecretResult;
  }
  return {
    ...sharedSecretResult,
    user: tailscaleCheck.user.login,
  };
}
```

The new config key is wired through config types, strict schema validation, sparse auth override merging, schema help/labels, and Gateway docs.

## Session invalidation when the flag changes
Enabling `requireTailscaleSharedSecret` at runtime is a security tightening, so live sessions that were validated under the looser policy must be dropped. Two changes make that happen through the existing shared-gateway session-generation machinery instead of a new mechanism:

- `src/gateway/server/ws-shared-generation.ts` folds `requireTailscaleSharedSecret` into the session generation digest, but only when the flag is enabled. Default deployments keep their existing generation, so already issued shared-auth device tokens survive an upgrade, while flipping the flag rotates the generation and forces re-authentication.
- `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/message-handler.ts` tags a tokenless Tailscale Control UI session with that generation so it participates in generation-based invalidation. Without this, a session accepted while the flag was off stayed connected after the operator enabled it. The narrow `usesSharedGatewayAuth` used for shared-auth device-token issuance is unchanged, so Tailscale sessions do not start issuing shared-auth device tokens.

The reload and RPC config-write paths already disconnect stale shared-auth clients through `resolveSharedGatewaySessionGenerationForConfig`, so both cover the flag toggle with no new call sites.

## Why this is the right boundary
Gateway auth already owns Tailscale Serve identity verification and shared token/password checks. Keeping the composition in `authorizeGatewayConnectCore` preserves the existing HTTP behavior, keeps the tokenless Control UI WebSocket behavior as the default, and lets existing shared-auth generation handling see layered successful sessions as `token` or `password` sessions for rotation and issued device-token tracking.

HTTP API endpoints remain unchanged because Tailscale header auth is still limited to the `ws-control-ui` auth surface.

## Verification
- `PATH=/opt/node/bin:$PATH node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/auth.test.ts src/gateway/startup-auth.test.ts src/config/schema.help.quality.test.ts src/config/schema.test.ts` passed 3 shards: 23 tooling checks, 464 Gateway checks, and 56 runtime-config checks.
- `PATH=/opt/node/bin:$PATH node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server/ws-shared-generation.test.ts src/gateway/server.shared-auth-rotation.test.ts src/gateway/server/ws-connection.test.ts` passed the session-generation, shared-auth rotation, and ws-connection suites, including the new `rotates the generation when requireTailscaleSharedSecret toggles` regression test.
- `PATH=/opt/node/bin:$PATH ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/gateway/server/ws-shared-generation.ts src/gateway/server/ws-shared-generation.test.ts src/gateway/server/ws-connection/message-handler.ts docs/gateway/configuration-reference.md docs/gateway/tailscale.md src/config/schema.help.ts src/config/schema.labels.ts src/config/types.gateway.ts src/config/zod-schema.ts src/gateway/auth-resolve.ts src/gateway/auth.test.ts src/gateway/auth.ts src/gateway/startup-auth.test.ts src/gateway/startup-auth.ts` passed.
- `PATH=/opt/node/bin:$PATH node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/gateway/server/ws-shared-generation.ts src/gateway/server/ws-shared-generation.test.ts src/gateway/server/ws-connection/message-handler.ts` passed.
- `PATH=/opt/node/bin:$PATH node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo` passed.
- `PATH=/opt/node/bin:$PATH node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-test.tsbuildinfo` passed.

## Real behavior proof: layered auth accept/reject
Behavior addressed: Tailscale Serve Control UI/WebSocket auth can require both verified Tailscale identity and the configured shared secret when `gateway.auth.requireTailscaleSharedSecret` is enabled.
Real environment tested: A real Node HTTP request produced the `IncomingMessage` consumed by `authorizeWsControlUiGatewayConnect` on pristine main d90c9a1ede8e9b098da0fd6ef17fb3432e82bfdf and on the patched `src/gateway/auth.ts`, which is byte-identical at the current head 95523d7b06b0dadbec7ef25b03d6631e3331b8d9; Gateway auth resolution, forwarded-header parsing, Tailscale identity verification logic, and shared-secret comparison all stayed in the production path, with only the local Tailscale daemon lookup supplied at the network boundary.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `PATH=/opt/node/bin:$PATH node --import tsx /tmp/tailscale-secondary-auth-proof.ts`
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main d90c9a1ede8e9b098da0fd6ef17fb3432e82bfdf)
without-shared-secret ok=true method=tailscale reason=none user=peter
with-shared-secret ok=true method=token reason=none user=none
# AFTER (patched auth.ts at head 95523d7b06b0dadbec7ef25b03d6631e3331b8d9, identical inputs)
without-shared-secret ok=false method=none reason=token_missing user=none
with-shared-secret ok=true method=token reason=none user=peter
```
Observed result after fix: With the option enabled, the live request without the shared secret is rejected, while the same Tailscale-verified request with the shared token is accepted and retains the Tailscale user.

## Real behavior proof: session invalidation on flag change
Behavior addressed: enabling `requireTailscaleSharedSecret` at runtime rotates the shared-gateway session generation and disconnects a Tailscale Control UI session that was validated while the flag was off.
Real environment tested: the production `resolveSharedGatewaySessionGeneration` (pre-fix source at 95523d7b06~1 vs the patched module) and the production `disconnectStaleSharedGatewayAuthClients` were driven directly. A tokenless-Tailscale client tagged with the flag-off generation was handed to the disconnect path with the flag-on generation required.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `PATH=/opt/node/bin:$PATH node --import tsx invalidation-proof.ts`
Evidence:
```
# BEFORE (pre-fix ws-shared-generation)
flag-off-generation=Vegtvfat-GImXHRUtacLE0G4KrYUyCqYooC6jHAYHlQ
flag-on-generation =Vegtvfat-GImXHRUtacLE0G4KrYUyCqYooC6jHAYHlQ
generation-rotates-on-flip=false
stale-tailscale-session-disconnected=false
# AFTER (patched ws-shared-generation)
flag-off-generation=Vegtvfat-GImXHRUtacLE0G4KrYUyCqYooC6jHAYHlQ
flag-on-generation =95pHHVcmKn8Yc3rf7aYNHcCaTSc_iHZ4ADhGtzybBzQ
generation-rotates-on-flip=true
stale-tailscale-session-disconnected=true code=4001 reason="gateway auth changed"
```
Observed result: pre-fix, the flag-off and flag-on generations are identical, so the stale Tailscale session is not disconnected. Post-fix, the generation rotates on the flip and the stale session is closed with `4001 gateway auth changed`. The flag-off generation is unchanged before and after the fix, so default deployments and their issued shared-auth device tokens are not invalidated on upgrade.

## What was not tested
No live Tailscale daemon request was made; the local daemon lookup boundary was supplied in-process. A full package build was not run because this change does not touch packaging or dynamic import boundaries.
